notes:
What's new in 0.1.76:
• Sign-in is safer against guessing. Sign-in now checks one password attempt at a time per address and per account, so many wrong guesses sent at once can no longer slip past the lockout. Your home network is exempt from the shared lockout, and one person's lockout no longer blocks everyone else.
• Sign-in no longer freezes the server. Checking passwords, reset codes, recovery codes and two-factor codes now happens without stopping everything else, so streaming stays smooth while someone signs in. Existing passwords keep working.
• A password changed during sign-in can no longer sneak the old one through. If a password was changed, an account revoked or two-factor switched on at the very moment someone was signing in, the sign-in is now refused.
• Saved keys and passwords stay hidden. The TMDB key, your email app password, notes and the OpenSubtitles key are no longer sent to the app's screens in readable form. Settings shows Saved, with Replace and Remove. A half-typed replacement is kept when you save another section, double clicks send one save, and a failed save tells you.
• Remote Desktop is stricter. Remote control now refuses to start while Beebo runs as administrator, and says so plainly. Control cannot travel over Beebo Relay, a wider set of proxy headers is refused, and the wording about the connection server is now accurate. Remote Desktop is still in development and off by default.
• Away-from-home tokens now say who they belong to. A paired TV can no longer be treated as the owner. Note: this needs the matching Beebo server update, which is being rolled out first.
• Safer file choices. Own ffmpeg, the nightly backup folder and Live TV guide and playlist files must now be picked in Beebo's own file box, and network paths are refused. Upload file names with hidden stream parts or Windows device names are refused. A saved network backup folder is shown as unusable.
• Safer connections for guides and playlists. If you approve a private guide address, it can no longer redirect Beebo to another address on your network. One shared check now decides what counts as a public address everywhere.
• Space Saver keeps accounts apart. Two accounts whose names look alike can no longer end up in the same folder. Nothing is moved or deleted; an old folder that two accounts could own is left alone until you choose.
• Pages load more safely. The library, music, photos, playlists, appearance, account and sign-in pages now carry a stricter content security policy.
• Pack for a trip shows size and time up front. The planner now shows an estimate of space and time before you start downloading.
• Fewer screens get stuck. Movies, TV Shows, Music, Podcasts, Audiobooks, Playlists, Requests, Movie Details, Playback settings, the Migration wizard and several others now show a message instead of staying on Loading or throwing a silent error when a call fails. A late answer no longer starts a video after you pressed Back in Surprise me.
• Smoother video streaming. Video pieces are streamed from disk when no speed cap applies, and a stalled player now stops its keep-alive timer.
• Logs hold less. Logs and the email log no longer keep tokens, addresses or subject lines.
• A paired TV gets a TV's reach, not the owner's. A TV signed in from away can play your library but can no longer open admin, account, API key or Remote Desktop pages. An away-from-home pass that does not say who it belongs to is refused.
• Account delete and privacy changes resist guessing too. Deleting your account, changing your viewing privacy, reset codes and two-factor steps now check one password attempt at a time, so many guesses at once cannot get around the lockout. A slow check keeps the account locked until it really finishes.
• Two more saved values are stored encrypted. The notes field for other logins and the DuckDNS token are now encrypted on disk like your other keys.
• Connection Doctor's firewall fix matches the installer. When it repairs the firewall it now adds the same rule the installer does, limited to Beebo itself.
• Your Home screen's "Open" buttons work. On the default Home look, the Open buttons on Continue Watching and the Fresh in Movies and Fresh in Shows rows now open History, Movies and TV Shows. Before, they opened nothing.
• Space Saver backups work again. Your computer was refusing every file the phone sent at exactly its stated size, so Space Saver backups failed. Fixed. Photo backup and Trip Journal links also no longer forget a file you already sent when the phone asks with a wrong size.
• Faster database for more households. On some Windows setups, a person with no ratings or favourites kept Beebo on its older data file instead of the faster database. Fixed; nothing was ever lost.
• Music and sign-in fixes. Pressing Stop while a radio mix was loading no longer starts it again. Reset codes count toward the same sign-in limit as passwords. The relay button now says it is on as a backup.
• Asks before removing things. Removing a library request or a title, and clearing items in History, Dashboard, Playlists, Podcasts, Radio and Live TV, now asks you to confirm first.
• Easier to use. With reduce motion on, lists and maps no longer scroll smoothly; more buttons are big enough to tap easily; the Watch Together panel in the player has clearer wording in all six languages.
• Many more screens tell you when something fails. Around 80 more screens were checked, including Settings, Music, Live TV, Parental controls, Upload, Library sharing, Cinema, Notifications, Add-ons, Backup, Trailers and the mini player. A failed save or load now shows a plain message instead of failing silently or staying on Loading; choices you change now stick instead of snapping back; and refused actions show words instead of raw codes. Bandwidth limit no longer shows Loading for ever when there is no limit.
• Not tested on real devices: Remote Desktop on a real screen. The installer is not code-signed.
• Built from commit 52119923, Oct 3, 2026, 2:10 PM Eastern.
